messages:
sanjay: Quick sync — after last night's canary we saw a cluster of tenant evictions and short-lived QoR drops. unsure if this is model-version regression or eviction churn. any strong hypotheses?

maya: ugh. do we have per-tenant blame signals? latency + perplexity spikes?

sanjay: we have latency spikes in the logs and higher mismatch rate on our eval prompts for tenant A. ops-bot posted eviction events: `evict: model=v2.17.3 tenant=tenant-A reason=out_of_memory`

devon: thread: are evictions happening because of memory pressure from quantized kernels or because rollout pinned a large-seq variant?

maya: +1 — we need to know which model variant was routed. current rollout metadata only has `model_ref` and `tag`. not enough to tie to kernel/quantization choices.

sanjay: proposal: add explicit fields to rollout metadata: `binary_variant`, `quant_mode`, `max_seq`, `kernel_profile`, and `deployer` so we can attribute resource blowups. also add `eviction_grace_secs` and `tenant_override` flags.

kai: sounds reasonable. can we keep it opt-in to avoid blowing up manifest size? default to inferred values when absent.

devon: we should also record a compact blame vector: small list of hypotheses attached to the rollout, e.g., `blame_candidates: ["kernel_mismatch","high_seq_runtime","memory_leak_candidate"]` so downstream analytics can aggregate.

maya: +1 but we need taxonomy and enum values, otherwise garbage. can we publish a canonical list in the schema?

sanjay: yes — i'll draft an enum: `resource_pressure`, `model_quality`, `client_behavior`, `runtime_bug`, `telemetry_gap`. each eviction event can reference the enum.

kai: also: add `observed_peak_mem_mb` and `kv_cache_size` snapshots at deploy time to make postmortems easier. lightweight numbers only.

devon: on rollback semantics — should rollback set a `blame_override` field to signal intentional revert (so auto-eviction systems dont reapply the same rollout)?

maya: we need that. otherwise automated healing will bounce. call it `rollback_reason` and `rollback_initiator`.

sanjay: ops question: how do we guarantee telemetry continuity when we add these fields? old entries will be missing new tags. analytics needs a migration path.

kai: answer: analytics should treat missing as `unknown` and use heuristics to backfill from runtime probes (if present). but Rollout API should also support a v2 manifest with `schema_version`.

devon: can we add a short `telemetry_anchor_id` that ties a rollout to a streaming telemetry timeline for quick joins?

maya: +1. that would let us join evictions -> logs -> eval-run quickly. name it `telemetry_run_id` or `telemetry_anchor`.

sanjay: ok i'll draft an RFC patch with concrete field names and enums. quick asks for the draft: keep fields small, optional by default, add `schema_version`, and include example manifest snippet in the RFC.

kai: thanks. can you also include migration notes for analytics and an example `backfill` query? we can then sync with SRE on alert tuning.
